name: Sharmin Sultana
title: PhD Student in Computer Science
tagline: I am a PhD student in Computer Science at the University of Massachusetts Lowell, developing healthcare-focused AI systems with an emphasis on clinical NLP and trustworthy models for electronic health records.
summary: I specialize in healthcare-focused artificial intelligence and natural language processing. My research centers on developing, fine-tuning, and deploying machine learning, transformer-based models, and large language models for analyzing clinical and biomedical data, particularly EHRs and social determinants of health. I work as a Research Assistant in the UMass BioNLP Lab under Prof. Hong Yu on opioid use disorder, overdose risk, and medication initiation among justice-involved U.S. veterans.
aboutExtra: Prior to my doctoral studies, I contributed to fair machine learning for health sensing and taught at the undergraduate level in Bangladesh. I am motivated by rigorous methods that improve patient-centered care and health equity.
researchInterests: Clinical and biomedical natural language processing
Healthcare AI and electronic health records (EHRs)
Trustworthy medical LLMs and uncertainty-aware systems
Fairness and robustness in health-related machine learning

news.text: New preprint: “Knowing When to Abstain: Medical LLMs Under Clinical Uncertainty” (arXiv:2601.12471).
Work on medical text generation, medical jargon identification, and health chatbots appeared in medRxiv, EMNLP workshops, and related venues—see Publications.
